explanations: The delivery_leg_minutes histogram is labeled with courier: leg.courier.id. Courier ids are unbounded, so every courier creates a new series per zone and vehicle, each holding a full set of buckets. As the fleet grows the in-process series map (and the metrics backend) grows without limit, causing memory growth, slow scrapes and high storage cost. Per-courier analysis belongs in logs or the database; the label should be dropped.
Both observe and inc come after await this.repo.save(leg); a rejection propagates out before either runs. Nothing records a fallback result.
requireOpenLeg throws "already closed" when deliveredAt is defined on the stored leg, so the second sequential call fails before any metric is touched.
deliveryResults uses labels zone and result, where result is "delivered" or one of the three failedReason values, giving four per zone. It never uses order ids.
